gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on portable CarPlay screens like Carpuride's the backup camera is matched to the screen model: Carpuride sells its rear camera ($30) per screen model, asks buyers to check the 'machine version number' in the screen's settings menu before ordering, and sells several screens (V92R 10.26-inch, C92, W904, W703) without a camera unless the buyer picks the '+backup camera' version.
standout_why: I compared against cartechtalk.com (names no connector, signal type or camera matching), gearnudge.com (lists Carpuride C3/C92/C98/W103 Pro 'with Backup Camera' and says to 'check whether the screen accepts a wired camera through a standard RCA video input', but never says Carpuride cameras are sold per screen model or that some console SKUs come without one), and carcody.com (explains composite vs HD and Kenwood/Garmin limits for in-dash head units, with nothing maker-sourced on portable screens). None quotes a maker's own rule on which camera goes with which portable screen.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's warning to make sure the box includes the camera, and it adds a rule: on a portable screen, buy the version that comes with the camera. If you buy the camera later from Carpuride, order the one for your screen model and version, not a generic RCA camera. The only in-dash Carpuride unit whose page says it takes a standard RCA AV camera is the YT09S double-DIN. That points shoppers who want to choose their own camera toward an in-dash unit, and shoppers who want the simplest setup toward a portable screen sold with its camera.
